name: Electric Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of not more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by Utah Code §41-6a-102 and regulated by §41-6a-1115.5, as amended by H.B. 381 (2026), whose changes took effect May 6, 2026, with its age and safety-course rules following on May 5, 2027.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can propel the bike on its own but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling, stops at 28 mph and must have a speedometer
A programmable e-bike qualifies only if it fully meets each class's rules in that mode, and must carry a label listing the classes it can operate in
Motor output of not more than 750 watts, fully operable pedals, cranks permanently affixed at the original manufacture, and fully operable as a bicycle without the motor

Anything designed, advertised or modifiable to reach 20 mph on motor power alone, with a continuous rated motor over 750 watts, foot pegs, or pedals only via a kit is not an e-bike; one over 750 watts or faster than 20 mph on motor power is an electric motorcycle

One modified or tampered with beyond the factory speed or power settings, or made to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone, becomes a high power electric device: it's ridden under motorcycle rules, is barred from freeways, and no one under 16 may ride it on a highway
Utah-based manufacturers and distributors must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point Arial stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Riders under 16 may not ride a Class 3; riders under 14 need a parent's or guardian's direct supervision to ride with the motor engaged on public property, a highway, path or sidewalk
Riders under 8 may not ride with the motor engaged on public property, a highway, path or sidewalk

Riders 8 to 15 may ride with the motor engaged on a highway only under a parent's or responsible adult's direct supervision or with a state personal electric vehicle safety certificate from an online course, and riders 16 and older ride unsupervised, Class 3 included
Since May 6, 2026, riders under 21 must wear a bicycle helmet meeting 16 CFR part 1203 on any class on a highway, except on a rented Class 1
No drinking alcohol or carrying an open container while riding any class (before May 6, 2026, only Class 2)
A peace officer who sees a rider under 18 commit a violation may hold the e-bike and release it only to a parent or guardian
Ridden under the rules for bicycles, and allowed on paths and trails designated for bicycles
A local authority or state agency may regulate or restrict e-bikes, or a single class, on sidewalks, paths and trails it controls
Not a motor vehicle or motorcycle: no driver's license or registration
